This is a corrected repeat.","body_html":"BINI has reached another global milestone, earning a feature from globally renowned media company Forbes following their successful debut at Coachella. Beyond the feature, each member drew praise for their distinct charisma and standout qualities, offering a closer look at their individual star power. In an article published on April 11 (PH time), Forbes senior contributor Jeff Benjamin highlighted the octet’s performance on one of the world’s most influential music stages. “BINI’s performance at Coachella 2026 made history as the Philippines’ first pop group performing at the taste-making festival,” the article began. Taking over the Mojave Tent, one of the festival’s largest and most prestigious stages, BINI delivered a high-energy set marked by sharp synchronization and commanding stage presence. The feature also underscored the group’s visual identity, describing their golden ensembles as a “modernized take on traditional Filipino fashion,” complete with elements like the salakot, before transitioning into colorful, festival-ready looks mid-performance. Beyond the spectacle, the article noted the strong reception from the crowd, pointing out how the group performed “to a massive audience where one could spot multiple Filipino flags,” signaling a powerful connection with fans even on international ground. Beyond the feature, Jeff’s real-time posts on X (formerly Twitter) provided a more detailed look into the performance, spotlighting moments that defined each member onstage. One post first highlighted the group’s stagecraft, with Jeff saying: “OMG that outfit change from 'Shagidi' to 'Zero Pressure' @BINI_ph,” emphasizing how even their transitions became standout moments in the set. Attention then shifted to Colet, whose visuals drew early praise. “The honey blonde on @bini_colet looks so amazing #BINI_CoachellaWk1 #BINI_Coachella,” he wrote, followed by another observation: “Yes, I think it's a septum piercing, it looks so good on her!” Mikha’s impact, meanwhile, was heard through her vocals. “I love @bini_mikha's vocal tone so much #BINI_CoachellaWk1 #BINI_Coachella,” Jeff said, pointing to a distinct sound that resonated across the festival setting. BINI leader Jhoanna’s introduction of the group became a defining moment, underscoring her ability to command attention from the very start. “Oh @bini_jhoanna greeting @Coachella and introducing group...the energy...you are SUCH A STAR, Jhoanna!,” he wrote. Sheena brought a different energy to the stage, capturing the infectious enthusiasm she radiated throughout the performance. “All the faces she's making, you can tell how much fun @bini_sheena is having on stage #BINI_CoachellaWk1 #BINI_Coachella.” Maloi’s presence, on the other hand, was described by Jeff as even more heightened in the Coachella environment, emphasizing her ability to dominate a globally recognized stage. “Wow @bini_maloi always owns the stage but it's like she's even more commanding here at @Coachella ...which isn't an easy stage to play at all!! So impressed #BINI_CoachellaWk1 #BINI_Coachella,” he noted. Jeff highlighted Stacey’s charm and how her look shone through both her visuals and performance. “Somehow @bini_stacey is even more charming with her cotton-candy pink hair 😍 #BINI_CoachellaWk1 #BINI_Coachella” Meanwhile, Jeff saw a sense of growth and composure with Aiah whom he first described as “tiny bit nervous” but then rose to the occasion. “OK at first I thought @bini_aiah seemed a tiny bit nervous (which is understandable!!) but she pulled it off flawlessly and really came through omg.” Gwen, on the other hand, delivered a performance that left a lasting impression on Jeff, with him even calling her a "true superstar." “I don't think I've been more convinced of what a true SUPERSTAR @bini_gwen is than after seeing her at @coachella tonight. The aura, the look, the vocals, the raps, the hair, the everythingggg #BINI_CoachellaWk1 #BINI_Coachella.” In another post, Jeff shared high-definition photos of the group, further delighting fans worldwide. Blooms were quick to react and share their gratitude to Forbes for seeing such qualities in the members. The Forbes feature adds to a growing list of international recognitions for BINI. Ahead of their Coachella debut, the group also spoke with the Los Angeles Times, which noted that BINI “takes care with its stages as a platform for Filipino culture — it champions local fashion designers in stage outfits, and its backup dancers are from elite troupes in the Philippines” while introducing global audiences to “where they come from.” Meanwhile, Rolling Stone had earlier included the group in its “20 Acts We Can’t Wait to See at Coachella” list, ranking them at 15th, before later giving positive feedback following their performance. “Through all of their accomplishment, BINI consistently manifested their Coachella debut for years now, often listing the milestone as a dream they hope to achieve one day. Now, they finally and triumphantly have,” part of Rolling Stone’s article read. Adding to the whirlwind of milestones, the group also received a surprise recognition from Billboard just hours before their set, as they were named among this year’s Global Force Award honorees at the Billboard Women in Music scheduled on April 29 (Pacific Time) at the Hollywood Palladium in Los Angeles, California. The post showed glimpses of their close bond, reflecting a love that deeply shaped Sheena’s dreams and determination.“oh Lord I'm missing her so much,” Sheena beganAngelyn was more than just a supportive parent; she was a guiding force in Sheena’s early passion for performing. Affectionately calling her “bebe,” Angelyn encouraged her daughter’s artistic growth by enrolling her in singing and dancing workshops. This early support eventually led Sheena to join a local dance crew in her teenage years. It was also Angelyn who convinced her to audition for Star Hunt despite Sheena’s initial hesitation, a decision that would eventually lead to her breakthrough and eventual place in BINI.But just as Sheena was closer to realizing their shared dreams, tragedy struck during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic when Angelyn passed away and did not get the chance to see her daughter as part of BINI.As Sheena stood on the brink of one of the biggest performances of her career at Coachella, she shared a series of deeply personal messages reflecting how much she wished her mother could witness the moment.“I'm so sure na she would've [risked] everything just to fly here and watch her bebe perform live sa Coachella. I know na you're always watching from above, but it still hurts to not see you or even hear your voice to say your good lucks and I love you sa akin. mas masakit kasi this has always been our dream, together,” Sheena expressed.“I hope I'm making you proud, Mommy. I pray to God that you have found peace and [rest] wherever you are right now, Mommy.”“I love you, mommy ko, I'm doing all of this for you,” she said, concluding her tribute by asking her mother to continue watching over her.Her emotional posts quickly drew waves of support from fans online, many praising her strength, honesty, and the deep love she continues to carry despite her loss.Despite the personal weight she carried, Sheena stood with BINI on one of the world’s biggest stages and helped mark a historic moment for Filipino music as the group became the first-ever Filipino act to perform at Coachella. Fresh from their historic debut at the festival, the Nation’s Girl Group has been recognized by Vogue in its article “The Best Celebrity Coachella Outfits of 2026 So Far,” highlighting not only their global stage presence but also their compelling visual storytelling through fashion. LOOK: BINI’s Coachella outfits were made of sustainable materials and real gold leaf, incorporating Filipino heritage into show-stopping looksIn the initial list curated by Vogue Senior Fashion and Style Writer Christian Allaire, which featured 25 artists, BINI secured the 17th spot. The feature spotlighted the group in their now-iconic teal siren outfits that perfectly captured the fluidity and grace of their performance. Designed by Raf Villas and styled by Ica Villanueva, the teal siren look served as BINI’s second outfit during their debut set. The ensemble offered a softer yet commanding presence, with hand-crafted details such as intricate weaving techniques, flowing tassels, and wave-like textures. Together, these elements emphasized movement and embodied the spirit of the ocean, all while maintaining a contemporary edge fit for a global stage. READ: BINI expresses pride and gratitude after making history at Coachella: ‘It just made us more proud to be Filipino’ The teal ensemble complemented their powerful opening look, where BINI channeled a bold Filipina warrior identity. Designed by Marian Zara in collaboration with Job Dacon and also styled by Ica, the gold outfits were rich in symbolism and cultural pride. Paired with traditional salakot hats, the look instantly grounded their international performance in Filipino heritage. According to Job, each golden warrior outfit was meticulously constructed using 20 to 25 sheets of real gold leaf and approximately two pounds of recycled plastic per member. Following the conclusion of Coachella’s first weekend, Vogue updated its list to include 39 artists, with BINI now in the 31st slot. The list also featured some of the biggest names in music and pop culture, including performers Justin Bieber, PinkPantheress, Addison Rae, KATSEYE, and Sabrina Carpenter. It also highlighted notable festival attendees such as BLACKPINK’s Lisa, sisters Kendall and Kylie Jenner, and Hailey Bieber, recognizing both artists and guests who brought standout style to the desert event. BINI’s fashion moment extended to Teen Vogue, where they were also included in “The Coachella 2026 Outfits From Weekend 1 You Absolutely Must See,” written by Beauty Editor Danya Momenian. The feature also included BINI’s teal siren looks and took note of BINI’s off-stage style, particularly during their appearance at the Revolve Festival and NYLON House afterparty following their much-talked-about performance. The octet embraced summer-ready fashion with modern bohemian ensembles in earthy tones of brown, white, and gray. This is a corrected repeat.","body_html":"BINI has reached another global milestone, earning a feature from globally renowned media company Forbes following their successful debut at Coachella. Beyond the feature, each member drew praise for their distinct charisma and standout qualities, offering a closer look at their individual star power. In an article published on April 11 (PH time), Forbes senior contributor Jeff Benjamin highlighted the octet’s performance on one of the world’s most influential music stages. “BINI’s performance at Coachella 2026 made history as the Philippines’ first pop group performing at the taste-making festival,” the article began. Taking over the Mojave Tent, one of the festival’s largest and most prestigious stages, BINI delivered a high-energy set marked by sharp synchronization and commanding stage presence. The feature also underscored the group’s visual identity, describing their golden ensembles as a “modernized take on traditional Filipino fashion,” complete with elements like the salakot, before transitioning into colorful, festival-ready looks mid-performance. Beyond the spectacle, the article noted the strong reception from the crowd, pointing out how the group performed “to a massive audience where one could spot multiple Filipino flags,” signaling a powerful connection with fans even on international ground. Beyond the feature, Jeff’s real-time posts on X (formerly Twitter) provided a more detailed look into the performance, spotlighting moments that defined each member onstage. One post first highlighted the group’s stagecraft, with Jeff saying: “OMG that outfit change from 'Shagidi' to 'Zero Pressure' @BINI_ph,” emphasizing how even their transitions became standout moments in the set. Attention then shifted to Colet, whose visuals drew early praise. “The honey blonde on @bini_colet looks so amazing #BINI_CoachellaWk1 #BINI_Coachella,” he wrote, followed by another observation: “Yes, I think it's a septum piercing, it looks so good on her!” Mikha’s impact, meanwhile, was heard through her vocals. “I love @bini_mikha's vocal tone so much #BINI_CoachellaWk1 #BINI_Coachella,” Jeff said, pointing to a distinct sound that resonated across the festival setting. BINI leader Jhoanna’s introduction of the group became a defining moment, underscoring her ability to command attention from the very start. “Oh @bini_jhoanna greeting @Coachella and introducing group...the energy...you are SUCH A STAR, Jhoanna!,” he wrote. Sheena brought a different energy to the stage, capturing the infectious enthusiasm she radiated throughout the performance. “All the faces she's making, you can tell how much fun @bini_sheena is having on stage #BINI_CoachellaWk1 #BINI_Coachella.” Maloi’s presence, on the other hand, was described by Jeff as even more heightened in the Coachella environment, emphasizing her ability to dominate a globally recognized stage. “Wow @bini_maloi always owns the stage but it's like she's even more commanding here at @Coachella ...which isn't an easy stage to play at all!! So impressed #BINI_CoachellaWk1 #BINI_Coachella,” he noted. Jeff highlighted Stacey’s charm and how her look shone through both her visuals and performance. “Somehow @bini_stacey is even more charming with her cotton-candy pink hair 😍 #BINI_CoachellaWk1 #BINI_Coachella” Meanwhile, Jeff saw a sense of growth and composure with Aiah whom he first described as “tiny bit nervous” but then rose to the occasion. “OK at first I thought @bini_aiah seemed a tiny bit nervous (which is understandable!!) but she pulled it off flawlessly and really came through omg.” Gwen, on the other hand, delivered a performance that left a lasting impression on Jeff, with him even calling her a "true superstar." “I don't think I've been more convinced of what a true SUPERSTAR @bini_gwen is than after seeing her at @coachella tonight. Ahead of their Coachella debut, the group also spoke with the Los Angeles Times, which noted that BINI “takes care with its stages as a platform for Filipino culture — it champions local fashion designers in stage outfits, and its backup dancers are from elite troupes in the Philippines” while introducing global audiences to “where they come from.” Meanwhile, Rolling Stone had earlier included the group in its “20 Acts We Can’t Wait to See at Coachella” list, ranking them at 15th, before later giving positive feedback following their performance. “Through all of their accomplishment, BINI consistently manifested their Coachella debut for years now, often listing the milestone as a dream they hope to achieve one day.
